text.tspan: IN CODE — shipped, tested, running in production
refuses over live data unless drained,
and repairs a half-built volume instead of rebuilding
one run per node, a second trigger exits 0
a backup must not depend on the leader being reachable
not mounted ⇒ REFUSE, never tar a live tree
postgres / mysql / mariadb are recognised from
their files, not validated from the host
pool ≥80% aborts loudly rather than shipping
never deletes a stack's last copies
restore opens ONE artifact, extracts it into the volume root
and prunes what it did not contain. The snapshot is long gone.
a systemd job, not a leader client — it finishes, and the
archive on disk is the record
NOT BUILT — RPO is one hour. The WAL stream that would
make it continuous (pg_receivewal over the container's trust socket) is designed, not written.
NOT BUILT — plan publisher and run-report endpoint.
NOT BUILT — restore writes into a live volume root,
so stop the stack around it.

svg.text: sudo pmcluster storage migrate (provision on an empty node)
loop file → PV → VG → thin pool → thin LV → ext4
mount at /var/stack/data — copy, verify, switch, keep the old tree
install units — pool, mount, and RequiresMountsFor on docker/daemon/agent
OnCalendar hourly, Persistent=true
flock -n /run/pmcluster-backup.lock
read cached plan.json when present
otherwise derive the plan from the directory layout
findmnt --mountpoint — is this really our LV?
fsfreeze -f /var/stack/data
lvcreate -s vg-pmcluster/data
fsfreeze -u
mount -o ro the snapshot
walk stack/ inside the frozen image
tar → backup-node-ts-stack-stack.tar.gz
manifest.json with sha256 and snapshot facts
verify — sqlite integrity_check
PUT artifact over WebDAV (127.0.0.1:7333, basic auth)
umount + lvremove
the store mirrors its bucket — SeaweedFS, not offen
retention — 48 h dense, one per day to 15 d, per stack
write run-ts.json
discover artifacts → backups rows
backup list / browse / restore
backup create (root) — run now instead of waiting for the hour
pmcluster backup-agent drill archive
extract + integrity_check, which is what proves restorability
rows discovered on the next pass
